# Authoring Context Pack V1

Plan 007 defines a deterministic, redacted export for external authoring. The boundary is always-on and admin-only by default.

The pack contains a versioned manifest, course and chapter metadata, published current Ideas, active source metadata, exact source excerpts, Idea provenance and relations, active learning objectives, safe content requirements, allowed benchmark summaries, and the authoring contract. An allowed benchmark projection includes its benchmark ID, dedicated ITB `referenceId`, exact `sourceLabel`, dataset key, version, checksum, and safe summary. The benchmark ID must never be used as the question source reference. The projection uses explicit fields and never serializes database rows directly.

Ideas must be published, current, and reviewed. Draft, stale, superseded, withdrawn, needs-review, or unreviewed Ideas are excluded. Source excerpts must belong to an active source version in the selected course.

Holdout benchmark stems, options, answers, solutions, embeddings, and identifying paraphrases are excluded. The manifest records only the number of holdout records excluded. Murid profiles, emails, enrollments, attempts, answers, mastery, chats, credentials, provider secrets, signed URLs, internal URLs, and user identity fields are excluded.

The content scanner fails closed on forbidden fields, secret canaries, signed URLs, internal URLs, and protected fixture values. New fields stay excluded until the allowlist and adversarial tests are updated.

The same snapshot ID, request policy, input content, creation timestamp, and retention timestamp produce identical entity checksums, pack checksum, and ZIP bytes. Files are sorted and JSON keys are serialized deterministically.

Private artifacts use the exact staging key `overhaul/<runId>/authoring-context/<packId>.zip`. The key is recorded in `audit_mutasi` with actor, policy version, source entity versions, holdout exclusion count, artifact checksum, correlation ID, and retention timestamp. The artifact is never exposed through a public URL. Rollback removes only explicitly named test objects by exact key.

```bash
bun --env-file=.env.staging run staging:preflight
bun --env-file=.env.staging run staging:test-authoring-context -- --run-id <runId> --course tutorial-pka
bun --env-file=.env.staging run staging:scan-context-pack -- --run-id <runId>
```
# Authoring Job Pack V1

Authoring Job Pack adalah workflow legacy untuk handoff berbasis ZIP. Workflow aktif sekarang menggunakan tiga skill MCP baru (`zyx-source-pack-mcp`, `zyx-idea-bundle-mcp`, dan `zyx-product-bundle-mcp`) dan tidak memerlukan download Authoring Job Pack atau Authoring Context Pack sebagai langkah antar-agent. Dokumen ini dipertahankan untuk kompatibilitas dengan workflow lama dan kontrak ZIP yang masih dibaca validator.

1. Upload satu Source Pack ZIP.
2. Tunggu analisis dokumen, unit, section, formula, visual, soal, dan pembahasan.
3. Pilih satu mata kuliah aktif.
4. Pilih satu atau lebih bab aktif.
5. Petakan setiap section sumber ke tepat satu bab. Jika hanya satu bab dipilih, seluruh section dipetakan otomatis.
6. Pilih keluarga produk. Artikel selalu aktif. Soal selalu dipasangkan dengan pembahasan, dan blueprint memerlukan soal.
7. Unduh `authoring-job-{name}.zip`.

Analisis dan pembuatan ZIP berlangsung di memori. Keduanya tidak menulis R2 atau database. Penyimpanan baru terjadi pada workflow upload dan konfirmasi Idea Bundle atau Product Bundle.

```text
manifest.json
authoring-job.json
source-pack/manifest.json
source-pack/documents/*.md
source-pack/coverage/*.json
contracts/authoring-job.schema.json
contracts/source-pack/manifest.schema.json
contracts/idea-bundle/*.json
contracts/product-bundle/*.json
instructions/external-authoring-workflow.json
```

Root manifest mendeklarasikan setiap file, ukuran byte, checksum SHA-256, job ID, Source Pack ID, dan course ID. File yang tidak dideklarasikan atau checksum yang berubah membuat pack ditolak.

`authoring-job.json` menyimpan label manusia dan ID teknis untuk course serta bab. Agent harus mempertahankan ID teknis persis, tetapi operator cukup bekerja dengan label di UI.

Setiap section mapping memuat document ID, section ID, judul, rentang source unit inklusif, chapter ID, dan label chapter. Semua section harus dipetakan tepat satu kali. Chapter yang dipilih tetapi tidak menerima section tidak disertakan dalam job final.

Attribution memakai sentinel `$UPLOADER` dan `$APPROVING_REVIEWER`. Zyx menyelesaikan sentinel tersebut menjadi identitas pengguna yang bertanggung jawab saat publikasi.

Pada workflow legacy, `source-pack-translator` menghasilkan Source Pack dan `package-source-pack.js` menetapkan seluruh entry ke mode `0644`; generic archiver dan packaging direktori skill dilarang. Validator JavaScript memverifikasi binary asli, count Markdown, marker, blok visual, dan quality report. Pada workflow MCP aktif, agent dapat memilih PDF yang sudah tersimpan melalui `source.list_files`, membacanya per halaman melalui `source.read_file`, lalu mengirim referensi terenkripsi sebagai `storedOriginals` ke `source.ingest`. Jalur file lokal tetap memakai input ephemeral `originals`. Kedua jalur menjalankan pemeriksaan yang sama, sedangkan stored originals juga mengikat token ke course dan chapter pilihan catalog MCP. Source Pack yang valid secara otomatis disimpan ke Cloudflare R2 dan dicatat di tabel `impor_bundle` dengan status `validated`, sehingga dapat diperiksa lewat `source.list_packs` dan `source.get_pack`, serta digunakan kembali langsung melalui `sourcePackId` pada `workflow.start` jika tahap Idea atau Product Bundle berikutnya perlu diulang.

Workflow legacy `zyx-product-authoring` menerima Authoring Job Pack dan Context Pack terbaru. Workflow MCP aktif melakukan pengecekan published Idea, version, semantic hash, dependency freshness, dan chapter scope langsung sebelum Product Bundle staging. Checkpoint publikasi Idea tetap wajib dan tidak dapat dilewati.

Seluruh packager dan validator yang dibundel dalam ketiga skill memakai file `.js` dan dijalankan langsung oleh Bun. Packager menolak file tambahan dan symlink, menetapkan mode ZIP `0644`, lalu menjalankan validator kontrak sebelum menulis hasil. Import ke modul kontrak `.ts` repository tetap diizinkan karena modul tersebut adalah implementasi otoritatif aplikasi, bukan script skill.

```bash
bun test tests/contracts/authoring-job-pack.test.ts
```

Gate tersebut mencakup Source Pack tanpa dokumen pembahasan, mapping lengkap, pack mandiri, dan deteksi file yang dirusak.

# Idea Bundle V2 Contract

Status: `TRANSITIONAL / LEGACY`. V2 remains readable and is the rollback submission contract while the V3 flag is disabled. New flagged authoring uses [Idea Bundle V3](idea-bundle-v3.md).

Idea Bundle V2 is a strict, ZIP-based import boundary for source-grounded Ideas. The workflow is always-on. The legacy JSON importer remains available as the rollback path.

The upload is parsed without extracting to a caller-controlled filesystem path. The reader rejects path traversal, absolute paths, NUL and invalid UTF-8 names, duplicate normalized paths, symlinks, executable content, nested archives, encrypted entries, ZIP64, multi-disk archives, unsupported compression methods, CRC errors, corrupt data, and decompression bombs.

Default limits are:

- Archive: 32 MiB.
- Entries: 256.
- Compressed or uncompressed file: 8 MiB.
- Total uncompressed content: 32 MiB.
- Compression ratio: 200:1.

Security failures use stable `ZIP_*` reason codes. JSON and entity failures use stable `BUNDLE_*` reason codes so operators can distinguish malformed input, missing dependencies, checksum drift, and conflicts.

The ZIP contains `manifest.json`, one JSON array for each declared entity type, and the UTF-8 source files named by `sourceVersions[].contentPath`. The current entity file types are `source_materials`, `source_chunks`, `ideas`, `provenance`, and `relations`. Paths are relative and every file is covered by the manifest checksum inventory.

The strict manifest contains:

- `bundleId`, `bundleType: "idea"`, `schemaVersion: "idea-bundle.v2"`, and `courseId`.
- Source material IDs, versions, checksums, and content paths.
- Entity file paths, entity types, checksums, and stable IDs.
- `creatorId`, optional `curatorId`, optional AI provider, model, and prompt version.
- `createdAt`, `bundleChecksum`, and an empty `conflicts` array.

Unknown manifest fields fail closed. The bundle checksum is deterministic over the manifest without its own checksum and the sorted checksums of all other files. Entity hashes use deterministic key ordering.

- Source metadata must match `sourceVersions` and the source bytes must match their checksum.
- Source rows must be active, Ideas must be publication-ready, and entity creator attribution must match the manifest.
- Source chunks must reference an existing source version, have exact offsets into normalized source text, and have a content checksum matching the chunk text.
- Ideas must belong to the manifest course, have unique IDs and stable keys, and use valid source and publication policy values.
- Published source-grounded Ideas require provenance. Provenance must reference an existing Idea and source chunk, cite the chunk checksum, and stay within exact chunk offsets.
- Relations must reference existing Ideas, cannot self-reference, and active prerequisite relations must be acyclic.
- Unresolved manifest conflicts, missing identities, invalid statuses, unsupported schema versions, and checksum mismatches are rejected before database writes.

1. An admin uploads a ZIP through `/api/admin/bundles/idea` with preview intent. The API validates the ZIP and returns an editable projection without writing R2, `impor_bundle`, `item_impor_bundle`, or canonical rows.
2. The admin reviews and edits Idea content, classification, provenance notes, and relation meaning. Stable IDs, course and chapter identity, source bytes, chunks, offsets, checksums, attribution, versions, and lifecycle state cannot be changed through the draft contract.
3. Explicit staging resubmits the original ZIP and draft. The server performs an allowlist merge, recomputes Idea semantic and generation hashes plus all entity and bundle checksums, repeats full validation, then records the final ZIP and inventory. An identical `bundleId` and checksum returns the existing import without new rows. A reused `bundleId` with a different checksum is blocked as `IDEA_BUNDLE_CONFLICT`.
4. A tutor may review an import only when assigned to its course. An admin may approve or reject. Review decisions are immutable and audited.
5. Only an admin can publish an approved import. Publication resolves legacy course and chapter identities, writes all source, chunk, Idea, provenance, and relation rows in one Turso transaction, and records `publikasi_bundle` plus mutation audits.
6. Vector work is inserted into `vector_sync_queue` as deterministic, conflict-safe outbox jobs for embedding-eligible source chunks and published Ideas. Source chunks use `source_materials` and Ideas use `canonical_ideas`; each job carries the content needed to build the canonical provider-neutral payload. No partial publication is visible after a transaction failure.

The review inventory lives at `/admin/materials/review?section=idea` (the legacy `/admin/bundles/idea` route redirects there). Published evidence is never deleted as a rollback mechanism.

The panel loads the immutable staged ZIP for review and displays every Idea, source excerpt, provenance role, relation, and AI generation label before approval or publication controls are available. External agents may use `$UPLOADER` for creator fields and `$APPROVING_REVIEWER` for curator fields; the values are resolved to real accountable identities only at publication.

The staging test covers valid upload, identical retry, conflicting retry, invalid path, invalid entity checksum, missing source, duplicate Idea stable key, forced partial publication failure, successful publish, and independent reconciliation. The successful Plan 006 evidence is stored at `artifacts/staging-overhaul/20260803-plan006-bundle-v5/plan-006-result.json` and the database reconciliation at `artifacts/staging-overhaul/20260803-plan006-bundle-v5/plan-006-reconcile.json`.

# Idea Bundle V3 Contract

Status: `ACTIVE` behind `FEATURE_STRUCTURED_ARTICLE_READER_V1` for new submission. V2 remains readable during transition.

Idea Bundle V3 adds a pedagogical outline to the source grounded Idea graph. The new entity file is `entities/learning-sections.json`, declared as `learning_sections` in the manifest. Source materials, source chunks, Ideas, provenance, and relations retain their V2 identity and checksum rules.

The ZIP, strict unknown field, deterministic checksum, source grounding, provenance, and relation cycle boundaries from V2 remain in force. V3 additionally validates learning section hierarchy, depth, slug, ordering, Idea coverage, and source chunk references.

Admin draft editing accepts only safe textual and ordering fields with `expectedRevision`. Stable IDs, Idea membership, provenance, and lineage cannot be edited. The server rebuilds checksums after an accepted edit. Per Idea review remains progress metadata and does not block overall Idea Bundle approval.

`workflow.get_contract`, validation, submission, Context Pack, and Job Pack advertise V3. Readers accept V2 and V3. When `FEATURE_STRUCTURED_ARTICLE_READER_V1=1`, new Idea Bundle submission must use V3. Disabling the flag restores V2 submission without deleting V3 artifacts.

# Product Bundle V2

Status: `TRANSITIONAL / LEGACY`. V2 remains readable and its block review endpoint remains a compatibility adapter. New flagged authoring uses [Product Bundle V3](product-bundle-v3.md).

Product Bundle V2 is the strict ZIP workflow for externally authored articles, diktat material, ITB example questions, solutions, flashcards, and assessment blueprints. Every question entering through this workflow is an ITB example. Zyx original questions are created through the normal bank question workflows and never through Product Bundle.

1. An admin uploads a ZIP at `/admin/materials/review?section=product` (the legacy `/admin/bundles/product` route redirects there). The first request validates and returns a complete editable projection without writing R2 or Turso.
2. The workspace maps product counts, dependencies, Idea and source traceability, options, reasoning, relations, curation, and every content block. Admins edit the renderable content and allowed relationship metadata in place while identity, source, version, and attribution fields remain locked.
3. Explicit save resubmits the original ZIP and browser draft. The server allowlist-merges edits, recomputes generation hashes and checksums, refreshes Article to Diktat lineage and product dependency hashes, repeats strict validation, then stores a draft ZIP and inventory.
4. A draft may be replaced with the same bundle ID and a new checksum, deleted, or published directly by an admin. Internal review evidence is created at publication and is not a separate public state.
5. Publication verifies current Ideas, source materials, excerpts, identities, and dependencies, then writes every product, link, dependency, canonical vector outbox entry, publication record, item status, and audit event in one transaction. Article, question, and solution content is routed to `published_articles`, `published_questions`, and `published_solutions`; Diktat, flashcard, and blueprint products do not use a generic `product` namespace.
6. A published bundle cannot be replaced or deleted. Withdrawal keeps history, marks canonical products inactive or retired according to the target table contract, marks the bundle and items withdrawn, and queues vector deletion for article, question, and solution content.
7. Identical retries are no-ops. A changed product version gets a physical versioned target ID such as `product-id:v2`; prior rows remain queryable.

Question publication writes the canonical `soal` row and an `ai_question_bank` compatibility projection with `origin: itb_example`, the event name, and the source reference. This makes the question available to existing quiz, tryout, PKA, and live-quiz paths without losing attribution. Withdrawal retires both projections. Attempt and submission snapshots retain the provenance so historical review keeps the original citation.

The only public lifecycle is:

```text
draft -> published -> withdrawn
```

The workflow is always-on. Learner and bank provenance labels render whenever provenance metadata exists. Legacy importers remain available as rollback paths.

Article products are compiled through `lib/materials/compiler.ts` after Product Bundle validation. The compiler orders prerequisite Ideas, normalizes each staged block into the typed article contract, and produces deterministic AST and Markdown output. Publication requires 100 percent required block coverage, source and Idea traceability for factual content, valid math delimiters, and current dependencies. Per-reviewer block status and notes are advisory admin metadata stored in `review_item_bundle`. Pending or `changes_requested` blocks trigger a warning but do not block approval or publication.

Block review metadata is never serialized into `manifest.json` or an entity file. It therefore does not affect product generation hashes, file checksums, or `manifest.bundleChecksum`. Restaging or discarding a draft clears its block review rows so decisions cannot attach to a replacement artifact.

Diktat products are derived from the approved article representation through `compileDiktatFromApprovedArticle`. The compiler never reads raw source independently for diktat content. Its report records the source article version and hash, removed block IDs, preserved core statements, formulas, Idea IDs, and source references. Any mismatch returns a stable reason code and blocks publication.

Every external Diktat product carries the Article lineage fields. Product Bundle validation and publication require the corresponding Article dependency. The existing `diktat_materi` and `artikel` tables remain unchanged; lineage is represented in the bundle and audit boundary without a schema migration.

The admin pre-staging workspace previews every supported product type, including each Article block and full Diktat content. The local preview scripts require `--dry-run` or an explicit read-only input and do not mutate staging resources.

```bash
bun --env-file=.env.staging run staging:preflight
bun --env-file=.env.staging run staging:test-product-bundle -- --run-id <runId> --fixture all
bun --env-file=.env.staging run staging:reconcile-bundle -- --run-id <runId> --type product
```

The staging fixture exercises all seven product types, identical retry, draft replacement, forced transaction failure, stale dependency blocking, holdout rejection, atomic publication, and versioned re-import. A new lifecycle run must also exercise draft deletion and withdrawal. Evidence is written to `artifacts/staging-overhaul/<runId>/plan-008-result.json` and `plan-008-reconcile.json`.
Use the legacy importers as the rollback path. Do not delete imported versions or audit records. If a published test bundle must be withdrawn, use the normal audited lifecycle operation.

# Product Bundle V3 Contract

Status: `ACTIVE` behind `FEATURE_STRUCTURED_ARTICLE_READER_V1` for new submission and structured review. V2 remains readable during transition.

An Article V3 stores `sections` and has no flat root blocks. A section contains stable identity, kind, title, slug, order, optional parent, learning objective, Idea links, source references, and semantic blocks. `topic` requires exactly one `learningSectionId`. `overview` and `summary` may synthesize multiple Ideas without one learning section.

Each block stores `contentMarkdown`, `blockType`, optional title, Idea IDs, and source references as fields. Metadata is never embedded in Markdown. The compiler preserves block types in the semantic AST and derives `artikel.contentMarkdown` deterministically for compatibility, search, and vector indexing.

- Every Idea is covered and traceable to a source.
- Every topic has a learning objective, core explanation, understanding check, and provenance.
- Examples, analogies, visuals, formulas, misconceptions, and warnings are required only when pedagogically relevant.
- Each topic declares a structured learning-time estimate for reading, examples, and practice. Completeness is judged against its objectives, not a fixed word count or reading-duration target.
- A chapter has overview, synthesis or summary, and a final understanding check.
- Pedagogy metadata binds objectives to explanation and formative-check blocks, declares prerequisites and symbols, and records whether a visual is required or not relevant.
- Required visuals use typed, non-executable payloads. A mathematically sampled graph is explanatory evidence only and never replaces an analytic proof.

`review_item_bundle` identifies `targetType` and `targetId`. V3 Article review targets `article_section`; the V2 block endpoint remains an adapter for `article_block`.

Admin edits require `expectedRevision`, accept only safe content fields, recompute generation hashes and bundle checksum, preserve approval for unchanged sections, reset changed section approval, and mark an Article to Diktat dependency `STALE`. Stable IDs, provenance, and lineage identity cannot be edited.

Publication requires the approving admin to have approved every Article section and all eight pedagogic criteria against the current content fingerprint and policy version. A different reviewer cannot reuse another reviewer's approval. Missing or stale approvals, stale dependencies, failed visual contracts, and missing, failed, or stale Diktat PDF evidence block publication. Publishing is transactional and idempotent.

The Diktat PDF worker compiles only the linked Article and Diktat revision, renders formulas fail-closed, records renderer and print-profile identity, verifies a 2 to 4 page PDF, then stores revision-bound evidence outside the ZIP. Admins may render, retry, and preview this artifact. Students may download the published PDF only when authorized for the course. The generic storage proxy cannot expose protected Product Diktat keys.

Admin and student previews use the same semantic section renderer. The admin model adds provenance, Idea IDs, dependencies, and review state. The student model omits all internal Idea and provenance identifiers.

When `FEATURE_STRUCTURED_ARTICLE_READER_V1=1`, new Product Bundle submission must use V3. The student material reader always prefers published canonical Article rows. Disabling the flag restores V2 submission without deleting V3 data or hiding published products.

| Environment | Engine | URL pattern |
|---|---|---|
| Development | SQLite (`dev.db`) | `file:dev.db` |
| Production | Turso (distributed SQLite) | `libsql://...` or `DATABASE_URL` |

Connection managed by `lib/db/index.ts` ; auto-detects production from `NODE_ENV`.

```bash
# 1. Edit db/schema.ts (Drizzle ORM ; sqliteTable)
# 2. Generate migration files:
bun run db:generate
# 3. Apply locally:
bun run db:migrate
# 4. Push to production (safe: backup + verify):
bun run db:push:prod
```

Never hand-edit files in `drizzle/`.

The table-by-table reference lives in [DB_SCHEMA.md](./DB_SCHEMA.md). High-level domains:

- **Auth** ; Better-Auth tables plus the canonical Indonesian identity layer (`pengguna`, `peran`, `pengguna_peran`).
- **Course and enrollment** ; catalog, cohorts, tokens.
- **Canonical source, Idea, product, assessment, mastery** ; the additive Indonesian learning-domain layer (`sumber_materi`, `potongan_sumber`, `ide`, products, evidence).
- **Content** ; MTDs, Knowledge Objects, assessment objects, profiles, policies.
- **Published assets** ; website materials, flashcards, diktats, course materials.
- **AI generation** ; jobs, question bank, usage events, traces, allowance leases.
- **Quiz and live classroom** ; templates (compatibility projection), attempts, feedback.
- **Mastery and analytics** ; learning events, mastery, streaks, recommendations, study paths.
- **Zyra runtime** ; learner profiles, preferences, attachments, proposals, operational telemetry.
- **Platform** ; blog, short links, forms, Meet sessions, media, push notifications.

- **SQLite stays** ; no Postgres. Turso for production scale.
- **Dual-hashing** ; `sourceHash` (raw content) + `derivedHash` (structured attributes) prevent unnecessary regeneration on cosmetic edits.
- **All timestamps** use `integer` (Unix ms) with `{ mode: "timestamp" }`.
- **Vectors** are stored externally in canonical Cloudflare Vectorize, not in SQLite. Legacy vector columns remain only as preserved migration history.

# Zyx Database Schema Reference

This document provides a detailed reference of the SQLite/Turso database schema defined in [db/schema.ts](../db/schema.ts). 

---

The Zyx ecosystem relies on SQLite locally (`dev.db`) and Turso in production. Migrations are managed via Drizzle ORM. 
- **Time Representation**: All timestamps are stored as SQLite `integer` values representing Unix milliseconds and are mapped to Javascript `Date` objects.
- **Foreign Keys**: Cascade deletes are used extensively to maintain integrity across course-specific content.
- **Coverage note**: `db/schema.ts` is authoritative; this document documents every table's columns. When this document and `db/schema.ts` disagree, trust `db/schema.ts`.

---

* `id`
* `name`
* `email`
* `emailVerified`: Boolean flag indicating whether the user's email has been verified.
* `image`: URL of the user's profile avatar.
* `role`: Temporary compatibility projection, which can be 'admin', 'teacher', or 'student' during the expand phase. Canonical authorization always uses `pengguna_peran`.
* `createdAt`
* `updatedAt`

* `userId`: Primary key and cascading foreign key to `user.id`.
* `emailEnabled`: Master control for all optional email categories.

Plan 008 reuses the same import, item, review, publication, audit, dependency, and vector outbox tables for Product Bundle V2. Migration `0081_numerous_gwen_stacy.sql` adds `review_item_bundle` as advisory staged review metadata with no backfill. Existing drafts therefore begin with every Article block effectively pending. Draft replacement rewrites the import inventory and R2 artifact and clears block review rows before publication. Publication inserts canonical article, diktat, question, solution, flashcard, and assessment blueprint rows after traceability and dependency checks pass. Withdrawal marks canonical rows inactive or retired according to their existing table contract and adds vector delete jobs. Question products are exclusively ITB examples and require `itbSource`, ITB curation, typed option IDs with deterministic correct markers, exactly one paired solution, and a HOT cognitive level for multi-Idea questions. Correct markers remain inside the private `soal.options_snapshot` grading representation and are redacted from runtime and vector content. Versions greater than one use versioned product IDs so prior rows remain queryable.

Migrations `0082_structured_article_expand.sql` and `0083_structured_article_review_targets.sql` add structured learning and Article tables, progress, generic review targets, and compatibility columns. V3 publication stores semantic rows and derived Markdown transactionally. V3 publication requires section approval from the same admin who approved the bundle.

Migrations `0087_curly_black_tom.sql` and `0088_talented_shinobi_shaw.sql` add Product Bundle pedagogic-review and PDF-evidence tables, then apply their lineage uniqueness, status, page-count, and Article-version constraints. They are additive to canonical product data; no existing Article or Diktat rows are rewritten.

Migration `0068_typical_warbird.sql` adds `origin`, `source_event_name`, and `source_reference_id` to both `soal` and `ai_question_bank`, with `zyx_original` as the non-null default and an origin plus event index on each table. Existing rows therefore remain Zyx originals without a data rewrite. Product publication validates ITB completeness before writing and creates the `ai_question_bank` compatibility projection. Product Bundle source and curation data are retained in the publication audit snapshot, while `soal_itb_referensi.soal_id` links the single source reference to its published question. Article to Diktat lineage is validated through bundle dependency rows and generation hashes. Live legacy quiz submissions use the existing `item_asesmen`, `jawaban_murid`, and `bukti_ide_jawaban` tables to append canonical evidence only after exact published-question and published-Idea checks pass.

Migration `0085_melodic_korvac.sql` adds `student_quiz_attempts.grading_status` with `not_required` as the compatibility-safe default and an index by template and grading state. It also adds reviewer identity, notes, timestamp, and revision fields to `jawaban_murid` for tutor quiz review.

Workers support the app:

Cloudflare tracing is enabled for each Wrangler-managed Worker through
`observability.traces.enabled`. This makes Worker runtime traces, including
Cloudflare Agent activity when an Agent framework is used, available in the
Cloudflare dashboard. No payload recording is configured by this repository.

```
workers/vector-api/
├── wrangler.toml
├── index.ts
```

- Exposes authenticated `/v2/upsert`, `/v2/query`, `/v2/delete`, `/v2/list`, and `/v2/get` routes
- Canonical `/v2/get` hydration is sent in batches of at most 20 IDs per request
- Production keeps the legacy `VECTORIZE` binding to `zyx-edu` for rollback compatibility
- Production binds `VECTORIZE_V2` to `zyx-vectors-production-v2` and `VECTORIZE_SEARCH` to `zyx-site-search-production`
- The two production indexes must use 768 dimensions and cosine distance, matching the canonical embedding profile
- Staging binds `VECTORIZE_V2` to `zyx-vectors-staging-v2` and `VECTORIZE_SEARCH` to `zyx-site-search-staging`; staging does not reuse production indexes
- Staging sets `RESTRICTED_SOLUTION_CAPABILITY` so published solution queries require the server-side capability check

#### Production provisioning gate

The Git merge does not provision Vectorize resources. Do not run a production deploy, backfill, or cutover until both production indexes pass the read-only checks below with dimensions `768` and metric `cosine`. If either index is missing or has incompatible metadata, stop and obtain an owner decision before creating or replacing it.

Run these commands from the repository root. They inspect account access, index configuration, and the rendered Worker bindings only:

```bash
wrangler whoami
wrangler vectorize list
wrangler vectorize get zyx-vectors-production-v2
wrangler vectorize list-metadata-index zyx-vectors-production-v2
wrangler vectorize get zyx-site-search-production
wrangler deploy --dry-run --env="" --config workers/vector-api/wrangler.toml
wrangler deploy --dry-run --env staging --config workers/vector-api/wrangler.toml
```

If an approved production index is absent, create it only after the gate has recorded the absence and the owner has approved the mutation. These commands are instructions, not commands to run during a merge:

```bash
wrangler vectorize create zyx-vectors-production-v2 --dimensions=768 --metric=cosine
wrangler vectorize create zyx-site-search-production --dimensions=768 --metric=cosine
```

The canonical metadata index allowlist is limited to eight properties, below Vectorize's ten-index limit. Create each property once on `zyx-vectors-production-v2`; `version` is numeric and every other property is a string:

```bash
wrangler vectorize create-metadata-index zyx-vectors-production-v2 --property-name=namespace --type=string
wrangler vectorize create-metadata-index zyx-vectors-production-v2 --property-name=courseId --type=string
wrangler vectorize create-metadata-index zyx-vectors-production-v2 --property-name=chapterId --type=string
wrangler vectorize create-metadata-index zyx-vectors-production-v2 --property-name=entityType --type=string
wrangler vectorize create-metadata-index zyx-vectors-production-v2 --property-name=status --type=string
wrangler vectorize create-metadata-index zyx-vectors-production-v2 --property-name=version --type=number
wrangler vectorize create-metadata-index zyx-vectors-production-v2 --property-name=accessClass --type=string
wrangler vectorize create-metadata-index zyx-vectors-production-v2 --property-name=language --type=string
```

Set the Worker secret after the production Worker and index bindings have been verified. Never put the secret value in shell history, Git, or this document:

```bash
wrangler secret put SHARED_SECRET --env="" --config workers/vector-api/wrangler.toml
```

#### Backfill and cutover order

1. Complete the read-only account, index, metadata, and dry-run checks above.
2. Provision only missing resources, then repeat the read-only checks and record the dimensions, metric, binding names, and metadata index list.
3. Configure the Vercel production values `VECTORIZE_WORKER_URL` and `VECTORIZE_SHARED_SECRET` through the encrypted environment settings. The application must not receive the secret from source control.
4. Run the production-approved canonical backfill from Turso using the fixed `canonical-content-v2` Gemini Embedding 2 profile, exactly 768 dimensions, and resumable run artifacts. Do not use a 1024-dimensional fallback or switch models.
5. Reconcile the Turso manifest against Vectorize IDs, dimensions, and allowlisted metadata. Require zero missing IDs, extra IDs, metadata mismatches, and dimension mismatches.
6. Run the canonical golden retrieval checks, including published-solution denial without `read:published_solutions` and success with that capability. Record the result before enabling production traffic.
7. Deploy only after all checks pass, then monitor the Worker and application error rates before completing the retrieval cutover.

Keep `zyx-edu` and the legacy `VECTORIZE` binding during the entire rollout. For rollback, restore the previously verified application and Worker version, disable the v2 traffic path according to the reviewed release procedure, and keep both new indexes intact for investigation. Do not delete or repoint the 1024-dimensional legacy index, and do not send 768-dimensional vectors to it.

The MCP endpoint is deployed as the Node.js route `/api/mcp/authoring` and uses the official Streamable HTTP transport. It is always available after deployment, but every request still requires a valid admin session or an MCP access token issued after an admin login. Source Pack ingestion requires original binaries for independent `originalSha256` verification; those binaries are not stored in the Source Pack ZIP. Originals may arrive as ephemeral base64 input or be resolved from encrypted stored-file references.

Prompt-only PDF authoring requires the active storage provider to implement server-side `download`. The default R2 provider and staging Wrangler R2 provider support it; a provider without download support fails closed. Only safe `courses/{course}/materials/*.pdf` keys are eligible. Page rendering uses the bundled `pdf-parse` worker under the existing Node.js runtime. No new environment variable, feature flag, database migration, remote URL fetch, or publication permission is introduced. Blob responses are limited to 32 MiB, stored originals to 50 MiB each, and aggregate originals to 96 MiB.

When enabling the endpoint, no MCP-specific static token or actor ID is configured. MCP authorization uses the existing Better Auth session through `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, `/api/mcp/oauth/register`, `/api/mcp/oauth/authorize`, and `/api/mcp/oauth/token`. The authorization code flow requires PKCE S256, checks the active admin role, binds the access token to the Better Auth session, and scopes it to the MCP resource. Default OAuth scopes are `authoring:read` and `authoring:stage`; supported explicit scopes include `authoring:review` and `authoring:withdraw`. Authenticated same-origin session connections receive all supported scopes. For clients without interactive OAuth support, an authenticated admin can call `/api/mcp/authoring/connection` to receive a per-session bearer token with a 30-day hard lifetime, bound to the live Better Auth session and active-admin role.

The endpoint exposes exactly two workflow choices, `idea_product` and `quiz_bank`; it does not expose a combined workflow or product-family selection. The quiz workflow exposes scoped Idea retrieval, accepts V2 question drafts with optional per-question Idea links, and writes canonical plus compatibility records as generated review items. `assessment.update_question` updates existing Zyx-original questions in the locked run scope and resets them to `reviewStatus=generated` for admin review (`authoring:stage`); ITB example questions are immutable and published or retired questions cannot be edited.

The MCP lifecycle surface provides inventory inspection, maintenance, and review tools:
- `authoring.list_imports` and `authoring.get_import` return staged bundle records, entity inventories, and review outcomes without exposing private storage keys or internal reviewer identity IDs (`authoring:read`).
- `authoring.restage_idea_bundle` and `authoring.restage_product_bundle` revalidate and replace staged bundles in place, resetting prior review decisions via existing lifecycle services (`authoring:stage`).
- `authoring.discard_product_draft` permanently deletes draft Product Bundles and their staging artifacts (`authoring:withdraw`). Published or withdrawn bundles cannot be discarded.
- `authoring.review_idea_bundle` and `authoring.review_product_bundle` record immutable review decisions (`approved` or `rejected`) with notes without publishing content (`authoring:review`).
- `authoring.withdraw_product_bundle` executes audited, idempotent, destructive withdrawal of published Product Bundles and retires canonical projections (`authoring:withdraw`). Idea Bundle withdrawal is not implemented.

Preserving the no-publication boundary: There is no `authoring:publish` scope and no publication tool. MCP submission can stage valid Idea and Product artifacts and generated questions, but no MCP tool can publish canonical content. Admin review and publication remain on the existing authenticated application boundary.

The current transport is stateless and does not require a database migration. OAuth authorization codes use the existing Better Auth verification store and are single-use. Signed access tokens have a 30-day hard lifetime, are derived from `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, carry the authenticated user and session identity, and are checked against the live session and active-admin role on every MCP request, becoming invalid earlier if the session expires or admin privileges change. The token is never permanent. Stored file keys encrypt their material and scope payload with AES-256-GCM and are also signed and limited to one hour. Short-lived workflow tokens carry the selected course, chapter, Source Pack checksum, and quality summary without exposing raw internal IDs. Canonical quality modules validate Source Pack originals and content, Idea coverage and duplicate candidates, and Product published-Idea scope, dependency freshness, and content density before staging. A later persistence phase can add run audit rows without changing the MCP tool contract.

The endpoint uses Streamable HTTP and returns JSON responses. MCP hosts discover the protected resource and authorization server metadata, then open the Zyx sign-in page. The authenticated principal must be an active admin. OAuth default scopes are `authoring:read` and `authoring:stage`; supported explicit scopes include `authoring:review` and `authoring:withdraw`. Authenticated same-origin session connections receive all supported scopes. For a host without interactive OAuth support, an authenticated admin can call `POST /api/mcp/authoring/connection` and configure the returned bearer token with a 30-day hard lifetime; the token is bound to the originating live Better Auth session and active-admin role, can become invalid earlier if the session ends or admin access is revoked, is never permanent, and cannot be issued by an unauthenticated caller.

For prompt-only Source Pack authoring, call `catalog.list_courses`, `catalog.list_chapters`, and `source.list_files`; read selected PDFs with `source.read_file`; then send the Source Pack to `source.ingest` with `storedOriginals`. Page reads accept at most four unique positive page numbers and return text plus 1280 px PNG images. Blob fallback is explicit and limited to 32 MiB. Stored files are limited to 50 MiB each and all direct plus stored originals are limited to 96 MiB. Ingested packs are stored in Cloudflare R2 and `impor_bundle` with status `validated`; existing packs can be listed via `source.list_packs`, inspected via `source.get_pack`, or referenced directly by ID in `workflow.start`.

`source.ingest` continues to accept ephemeral base64 `originals` for local files. Direct and stored originals may be mixed when document IDs are unique. Stored references are revalidated against their current course, chapter, update timestamp, checksum, safe PDF key, and R2 bytes; their Source Pack token is rejected if `workflow.start` selects another course or chapter. Validated packs persist to R2 and `impor_bundle` automatically, enabling resumption across sessions if subsequent Idea or Product Bundle authoring fails. Idea and Product tools return canonical technical and content quality reports and refuse staging when blocking issues remain. For `quiz_bank`, call `assessment.list_ideas` after `workflow.start`, send `question-bank-draft.v2` to `assessment.validate_quiz_draft`, then submit the same JSON to `assessment.submit_quiz_draft`. Each question may omit `ideaLinks`; non-empty links require positive weights summing to one. `assessment.update_question` updates existing Zyx-original questions in scope and returns them to `reviewStatus=generated` for admin review (`authoring:stage`); ITB example questions are immutable and published or retired questions cannot be edited.

The MCP lifecycle surface provides inventory inspection, maintenance, and review tools:
- `authoring.list_imports` and `authoring.get_import` inspect staged bundles, validation reports, and review decisions without exposing storage keys or reviewer IDs (`authoring:read`).

- `authoring.withdraw_product_bundle` executes audited, idempotent, destructive withdrawal of published Product Bundles (`authoring:withdraw`). Idea Bundle withdrawal is not implemented.

Preserving the no-publication boundary: There is no `authoring:publish` scope and no publication tool. Feature flags are exception-based rollout controls, not a requirement for every new capability. Keep a capability always-on when it is foundational, stable, part of core authorization, retrieval, assessment, learning, or pedagogy, or when a flag would only mirror an implementation boundary. Consider a flag when the capability is optional, experimental, expensive or externally side-effectful, audience or environment specific, or needs a reversible kill switch.

Before adding or removing a flag for a new capability or material behavior change, the agent or maintainer must ask the owner to choose always-on or flag-gated when the request has not already decided it. The decision records the proposed key, reason, default, scope, rollback behavior, owner, and removal condition. A temporary operational flag may protect a high-risk migration or provider boundary, but it is not automatically a product flag or an admin catalog entry.

A retained flag is active only when its value is `"1"` or `"true"`; an absent value keeps that optional capability hidden. Foundational behavior is always-on and intentionally has no env flag.

Current approved vital flags (< 10 flags retained for high-impact runtime control):

| Flag | Feature | Scope |
|------|---------|-------|
| `FEATURE_PKA` | Tutorial PKA campaign course & registration gate | Academic / Campaign |
| `FEATURE_REFLECTION_EMAIL` | Weekly reflection email batch dispatch gate | Academic / Resend |
| `FEATURE_LIVE` | Real-time interactive classroom & Cloudflare Worker switch | Quiz & Live |
| `FEATURE_DIKTAT_AI` | LLM quota protection for Diktat AI audit suggestions | AI Architecture |
| `FEATURE_ZYRA_IMAGE_INPUT_V1` | Learner multimodal image input & vision quota switch | AI Architecture |
| `FEATURE_ZYRA_SEMANTIC_CACHE_V1` | Vectorize semantic cache kill switch for semantic drift | AI Architecture |
| `FEATURE_DRIVE_EDITOR_SYNC` | Auto-grant editor permission synchronization on Drive | Platform / Admin |
| `FEATURE_STRUCTURED_ARTICLE_READER_V1` | Structured V3 authoring, submission, and review rollout | Academic / Admin |

> Foundational features (Tutor Portal & Overhaul, Remediation, Adaptive Quiz, Concept Graph, Interactive Material, Weekly Reflections, Tutor Analytics, Question Generator Critic, Idea & Product Bundles, Authoring Context, Zyra Allowance & Provider Router, Learning Canvas, Selection-to-Ask, Zyra Pet, AI Ops, Media Library, Link Library, Form Presets) are now mature and always-on by default, secured by role-based authorization (RBAC).

The admin flag page reads this catalog from `lib/feature-flags.ts`; arbitrary `FEATURE_*` variables are not surfaced. `FEATURE_STRUCTURED_ARTICLE_READER_V1` defaults to disabled. It is owned by Akademik dan Konten together with the Zyx platform owner. Its rollback disables V3 authoring, submission, and review selection without deleting V3 data or hiding products that are already published from students. See [the rollout runbook](operations/structured-article-v3-rollout.md). Decommissioned flags have been removed from `lib/env.ts`, runtime schemas, environment files, and operational scripts.

- **DB schema**: `db/schema.ts` only. Edit → `bun run db:generate` → `bun run db:migrate`. Never hand-edit `drizzle/`.
- **Auth**: Better-Auth (credentials + Google OAuth). Canonical access roles: `admin`, `tutor`, `murid`; `user.role` remains a legacy compatibility projection during expand.
- **AI calls**: All Gemini traffic routes through Cloudflare AI Gateway when `CF_AI_GATEWAY_URL` is set.
- **Cost rule**: AI quota is spent only on tutoring, mistake feedback, and content generation. Streaks, recommendations, study paths, reflections are deterministic SQL + logic.

Exports route through `lib/google-sheets.ts` and `POST /api/admin/export-spreadsheet`. The spreadsheet is updated in place; the app owns only the data block at A1 (header + data rows) and writes it with an explicit `GridRange`, so admin edits in the reserved manual zone (columns right of the data, rows below it) are never overwritten.

Before an overwrite the current grid is read and diffed against `export_spreadsheets.last_written_fingerprint` plus the stored row/column counts. Detected manual edits inside the owned block, growing rows over manual cells, or growing headers over manual columns return `needsConfirmation` with `block_modified`, `manual_rows`, or `manual_columns` codes. Client callers use `useSpreadsheetExport` (`components/admin/spreadsheet-export.tsx`) to show a confirm dialog and re-send with `confirmOverwrite: true`. New spreadsheets store the baseline so later re-exports can warn precisely; legacy sheets without metadata infer the previous block from the current grid on the first re-export.

Set `FEATURE_DRIVE_EDITOR_SYNC=1` to grant every active admin email `writer` access on exported spreadsheets, Google Forms, recording files, transcripts, and new export folders.

Meet member provisioning uses `https://meet.googleapis.com/v2beta/spaces/{space}/members`. The Google Cloud project and OAuth principal must be enrolled in the Google Workspace Developer Preview Program, and the refresh token must include the Meet space settings scope. Without Preview access or the scope, space creation still succeeds but the admin UI reports each co-host or invitee grant that failed.
